title: The Simpleton and the Sharper

full_text:
A country simpleton was walking to the market of Baghdad, leading a handsome fat ram by a rope, hoping to sell it to buy new shoes and winter clothing.

A cunning sharper observed the simpleton and resolved to swindle him without using violence. The sharper enlisted two companions and positioned them at three successive crossroads along the country road.

When the simpleton reached the first crossroad, the first accomplice looked at the ram with astonished eyes and called out: 'Good day, brother! Why are you leading that dirty, mangy dog by a rope?'

The simpleton frowned and replied: 'Are you blind, friend? This is not a dog; this is a fat ram with horns and thick wool!' The stranger shook his head with pity and walked away.

At the second crossroad, the second accomplice stepped up and shouted: 'Ho, traveler! How much do you ask for that scrawny greyhound?'

The simpleton began to feel uneasy. He examined the ram, felt its wool and curved horns, and muttered: 'Surely it is a ram... or have my eyes been touched by an enchantment?'

At the third crossroad, the chief sharper stepped forward, raised his hands in horror, and scolded: 'O man of little sense! It is unlawful to lead such an unclean, mangy hound along the public highway! Let the beast go before the magistrate fines you!'

Overwhelmed by the agreement of three separate strangers, the simpleton abandoned all faith in his own senses. Believing that his prize ram had truly been transformed into an unclean dog by sorcery, he dropped the rope in terror and fled toward the city!

The three sharpers immediately gathered the fat ram, led it to the butcher's quarter, and sold it for twenty silver dirhams, laughing at how easily a man surrenders his truth when he allows false consensus to overrule his own eyes.
moral: Do not let deceptive consensus shake your confidence in what your own eyes clearly see.
